## 1. Reverse complement

DNA is double-stranded, and a read can come from either strand. The *reverse complement* reads the other
strand: complement every base (`A↔T`, `C↔G`) and reverse the result. Keep `N` (unknown base) as `N`.

```python
def reverse_complement(seq: str) -> str:
    ...

# tests
assert reverse_complement("AAAACCCGGT") == "ACCGGGTTTT"
assert reverse_complement("") == ""
assert reverse_complement("ACGTN") == "NACGT"
assert reverse_complement(reverse_complement("GATTACA")) == "GATTACA"
```

## 3. The longest substring

See also <https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-length-of-repeated-subarray/description/>

```python
def longest_common_run(a: str, b: str) -> int:
    ...

# tests
assert longest_common_run("ACCGGTGGAACCGGTAACACCCAC", "ACCGGTAACCGGTTAACACCCAC") == 10
assert longest_common_run("ABC", "XYZ") == 0
assert longest_common_run("GATTACA", "GATTACA") == 7
assert longest_common_run("", "ACGT") == 0
```

## 4. Longest common subsequence

A *subsequence* may skip characters; a substring may not. Return the length of the longest common

See also <https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-common-subsequence/description/>

```python
def lcs_length(a: str, b: str) -> int:

# tests
assert lcs_length("ABCBDAB", "BDCABA") == 4
assert lcs_length("AGGTAB", "GXTXAYB") == 4
assert lcs_length("ACGT", "") == 0
assert lcs_length("GATTACA", "GATTACA") == 7
```

## 5. Maximum subarray --- Smith-Waterman in one dimension

Given a list of numbers, return the largest sum of a contiguous, non-empty slice.

Hint: <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_subarray_problem#Kadane's_algorithm>

See also: <https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-subarray/description/>

```python
def max_subarray(nums: list[float]) -> float:
    ...

# tests
assert max_subarray([-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4]) == 6
assert max_subarray([1]) == 1
assert max_subarray([-3, -1, -2]) == -1          # non-empty: the best single element
assert max_subarray([5, 4, -1, 7, 8]) == 23
```
